articles.summary: India is seeking to make economic growth more resource-efficient and resilient by expanding recycling infrastructure, strengthening markets for recycled materials and bringing more producers into a regulatory framework for waste management, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav said on Tuesday.Addressing the inaugural session of the 10th World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF 2026) in Gandhinagar, Yadav said circularity should be viewed not simply as an environmental policy but as a way to improve the quality and sustainability of economic growth."The choice before us is not between growth and the environment. The real opportunity is to make growth itself more resource efficient, more resilient and more sustainable, and this is precisely what WCE provides," he said.Yadav said India has made progress in expanding recycling capacity, encouraging new recycling technologies, developing markets for recycled materials and promoting eco-design and circular procurement. He said the success of a circular economy should not be measured only by the quantity of waste recycled, but by the amount of economic value preserved."The true measure of a circular economy will not be how much waste is recycled, but how little value we allow to be wasted," he said.India expands regulatory framework for waste and recyclingThe government's circular economy strategy is being built around regulatory reforms and digital compliance systems covering multiple waste streams, Yadav said.Over recent years, India has strengthened its waste-management framework under the Environment Protection Act, 1986, with rules covering plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste."Our objective is clear - waste should no longer be seen as the end of a product's journey but as the beginning of another resource cycle. One of the most transformative reforms has been the introduction of extended producer responsibility (EPR)," he said.The EPR framework shifts responsibility beyond conventional regulation by requiring producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life.As of August, more than 83,000 producers and 4,802 recyclers were registered under the EPR framework, Yadav said. Nearly 482.24 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, while more than 422 lakh metric tonnes were covered through EPR certificate generation.He said the figures represented more than regulatory compliance."They represent materials recovered, resources conserved, technology deployed and livelihood created," Yadav said.From recycling to consumptionYadav said regulation alone would not be enough to establish a circular economy, arguing that changes in consumption patterns were equally important."A circular economy cannot be built only at the recycling plant; it must begin at the marketplace, continue at our homes, and ultimately become a habit in our daily life," he said.He linked this approach to Mission LiFE, introduced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which promotes more deliberate and mindful use of resources rather than wasteful consumption.Yadav also framed circularity as an extension of practices that have long existed in India, including repairing, reusing and recovering materials rather than discarding them."For India, circularity is not a new destination; it is a new way of looking at old wisdom. We are not merely adopting a new economic model, we are modernising values that have served our society for generations," he said.He cited neighbourhood trades such as cobblers, tailors, watch mechanics and cycle repairers as examples of traditional systems that kept products in use for longer.India steps up global circular economy cooperationYadav said circularity requires cooperation across countries and industries, with knowledge, technology and finance needed to move the transition beyond individual sectors.India's international efforts include cooperation with the European Union on resource efficiency and circular economy, identified as areas of cooperation in the India-EU joint declaration of July 2020.During India's G20 presidency, the country also launched a resource-efficiency and circular-economy industry coalition aimed at encouraging industrial action and collaboration.India's cooperation with Germany through the joint working group for waste and circular economy and the Indo-German Environment Forum has focused on practical solutions, Yadav said.(With inputs from PTI)

articles.title: 3 countries threaten to break away from UK
articles.summary: The leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland signed a pact Monday that threatens to lead to the breakup of the United Kingdom.The first ministers of the three semiautonomous regions of the UK told Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his government to prepare for constitutional change and that their future lies with the European Union."For people watching across these islands - for people watching around the world - there could be no clearer sign that Westminster's time is coming to an end," they said in a memorandum of understanding, referring to Parliament.The announcement came about 48 hours after US President Donald Trump waded into the waters of the politically contentious issue when he said he would "love to see" a reunified Ireland during a trip to visit his golf course hosting the Irish Open.It's the first time the leaders of all three countries are either from pro-independence parties, or pro-unification in the case of Northern Ireland, which was partitioned and remained part of the UK when Ireland won independence from Britain over a century ago.Burnham's spokesperson brushed aside the threat and said the prime minister strongly believes in the union and was more focused on lowering the cost of living than dealing with constitutional debates."The United Kingdom is at its best when people come together around our shared values and problem-solving, rather than division," Tom Wells said.Nicola McEwen, director of the University of Glasgow Centre for Public Policy, said the summit was symbolically important but has no legal significance."I don't see the threat to the union being bigger today than it was yesterday," McEwen said.In the late 1990s, the UK passed legislative acts that decentralised government through the process of devolution, giving each country except England some level of policy independence and self-governance through their own parliaments.But tensions have remained with the UK-wide government in London, which retained control over national issues and those concerning England.Scotland's John Swinney and Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill called for independence referendums in their countries, while Rhun ap Iorwerth did not provide a timetable for one in Wales.The three leaders appeared in their political capacity, rather than their official one, possibly because O'Neill is in a power-sharing government with the Democratic Unionist Party.Northern Ireland's Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly, of the DUP, accused O'Neill, of the Sinn Fein party, of "weaponising" the role of first minister by signing the agreement."I am first minister in the north of Ireland," O'Neill replied. "This is about historic change happening all around us."Scotland tried unsuccessfully to break away in 2014, with voters rejecting a referendum 55 per cent to 45 per cent. But McEwen said support for Scottish independence has grown since Brexit, in which the UK formally left the European Union in January 2020, following a referendum in June 2016.Swinney, leader of the Scottish National Party, said he believed voters would now vote for independence if the UK government approved a referendum.Burnham told Parliament last week he would allow such a vote to be held if there was a "clear consensus" in Scotland, but later sent Swinney a letter saying a vote was "off limits".The 1998 Good Friday peace accord that ended three decades of sectarian violence in Northern Ireland known as "The Troubles," requires a vote on unification if polls there indicate it would likely pass, a threshold the UK government says has not been met. Ireland would also have to approve the change in a referendum.Burnham has made devolution a major theme since taking office less than two months ago, but his focus has been on regional governments across England, a reflection of his years as mayor of Greater Manchester.Swinney tried to turn Burnham's ideology to his advantage, saying his frequent talk of devolution "leads you to the logic of recognising the right of the people of Scotland, in my case, to decide their own future".Beyond any threat of departing the union, McEwen said the greatest impact of the three joining forces could be that they agreed to cooperate with each other routinely and that could help to exert more influence on the UK government."It does keep on the agenda that question about, well, if the United Kingdom is a union based on consent, what is the pathway where it looks like that consent may no longer be there?" McEwen said. "Any UK government has been very reluctant to engage in that discussion."
